t: The two sides disagreed about where the border lay: the Japanese held that it was the Khalkhin Gol, the Mongolians and Soviets that it ran 16 kilometres to the east, just east of Nomonhan.
Zhukov's offensive of 20 August pinned the Japanese in the centre and swept armoured units round both flanks, trapping the Japanese 23rd Infantry Division when the wings linked up on 25 August.
Japanese casualty figures range from about 19,714 in the Sixth Army's medical data to 35,000 to 36,000 reported by a minister, and the Soviet claims for them rose from 29,085 to 61,000.
dyk: The Japanese record the fighting as the Nomonhan Incident, after Nomonhan Burd Obo, yet it involved aircraft, tanks and tens of thousands of troops, and it ended only with a cease-fire.
ev: The Soviet Union and Mongolia sign a Mutual Assistance Pact, allowing Soviet troops into Mongolia
A Mongolian cavalry unit is driven back across the Khalkhin Gol by Manchukoan cavalry
Soviet and Mongolian forces surround and destroy the Azuma force
The Japanese attack in two prongs, but both are thrown back by 9 July
A second large Japanese assault on the Kawatama Bridge is called off on 25 July
Zhukov opens his offensive with artillery and 557 aircraft
The Soviet wings link up near Nomonhan and trap the Japanese 23rd Infantry Division
The Soviet Union and Japan agree a cease-fire

f.date: 11 May to 15 September 1939; the cease-fire agreed on 15 September took effect at 1:10 pm on 16 September. The main Soviet offensive began on 20 August
f.place: Along the river Khalkhin Gol near Nomonhan, on the disputed border between the Mongolian People's Republic and Manchukuo, in present-day Mongolia and China
f.sides: The Soviet Union and Mongolia under Georgy Zhukov, with about 50,000 Soviet and Mongolian soldiers in the attack on the east bank on 20 August; Japan and Manchukuo, with the Kwantung Army's 23rd Infantry Division under Lieutenant General Michitarō Komatsubara at the point of contact
f.outcome: Soviet victory: the Japanese forces on the Mongolian side of the border were destroyed by 31 August, and a cease-fire followed on 15 September.
